data.narrative:
Atomic Machines, a Series A semiconductor company founded by Jeff Holden, has raised $144M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies, with 3 direct Series A/B peers: Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression anchors to the $144M total raised as a base proxy, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $288M. Peer-median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a $2.0B midpoint, with a range of $1.0B–$2.3B. Public-comp anchoring (18.9x median P/S across the semiconductor tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, common among private companies.

The triangulated range is $245M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects tension between conservative capital-raised proxies and peer-benchmark pricing in a capital-intensive sector where recent Series A fundings have commanded valuations substantially above deployment-to-date. Key uncertainties include undisclosed revenue, technology differentiation relative to named peers, and stage-progression velocity in semiconductor infrastructure markets.
